_doc: Gig kinds and board tuning for the fixer board (M6, M9 P3; the Mission Builder, SPM p.28, data/gen/mission_builder.json). Each offer rolls a Mission Type (its objective gives the kind: templates list the kinds and a plain label for each), a security level weighted by the crew's best Reputation (CPR p193, per character; rep_for_security), then a canon Night City location of that level (data/world/locations.json: hooks naming the kind first, else places whose gigs include it) and a Fixer working its district (data/world/fixers.json; fixer_tags: which deals_in tags suit each kind, weighted up). The Mission Builder then adds the client, the focus item, the payment and the twist hook (MissionBuilder). The title is the mission type's label and the location; the blurb is '<Fixer> has work at <Location> (<District>): <mission framing> <hook>'. Every offer is at a canon location (owner ruling 2026-11-04: no generic offers): when no place fits the mission's kind at the rolled level or below, the other kinds are tried. Unique offers (spec: 'occasional unique offers' from fixers who trust you) appear once the crew's best Reputation reaches unique_rep, at one of the target's own places (else a canon place for the job); their titles/blurb fill {fixer}, {corp}, {gang}, {item_short} (the focus item) and {place} (the location's name); focus: the focus item the job is about (category/id), else one is rolled for the place. Target factions come from data/world/factions.json (each faction lists the gig kinds it can be the target of); {corp}/{gang} slots are filled with the target's name, and titles naming the other kind of slot are skipped. Complications are no longer here: the book's Hardened complication tables (data/rules/npcs.json) are rolled at gig start (Complication).
_pay: The job's rate by security level, before the payment step (MissionBuilder) splits it: CPR core p.381 pays an Easy job 500eb, a Typical 1,000eb and a Dangerous 2,000eb per person; levels 1-3 are those, for the two-person crew a campaign starts with. HOUSE-RULE: flat per gig, not per head, so a bigger crew splits the same pay (the book's per-person rate would make every hire pay for itself).

unique_templates.blurb: {fixer} trusts you with this one. A {corp} prototype is in storage tonight; bring it back. Double pay.
{fixer} wants the {gang} gone for good. Their main crew is at the {place}. Double pay.
{fixer}'s client wants {corp}'s {item_short}. Expect a deep NET and heavy Black ICE. Double pay.

tower._why: HOUSE-RULE (owner 2026-11-08: tower gigs are rare and gated to later progression, with a good mix of high-rise and ordinary gigs). Once the crew's best Reputation reaches rep (4: known all over the local area, CPR p.193), one board in chance_in carries one tower offer (Campaign._tower_offer), in place of its last ordinary offer. A tower job pays its level's rate times pay_mult (the ride up is part of the risk). One tower gig in day_in plays by day, the rest at night (owner, V1 verdicts 2026-11-09: some campaign tower gigs by day; night stays the campaign look), drawn from the gig's seed and kept on the gig as sky (Campaign.tower_sky).
